text: Three Types of Jitter Implementations
speaker: Simon

text: 1. Basic RTT Jitter (Simple Consecutive RTT Difference)
speaker: Simon

text: This method calculates jitter based on the difference between consecutive ICMP Echo RTT measurements.
speaker: Simon

text: Send continuous ICMP Echo requests
speaker: Simon

text: Record each RTT value
speaker: Simon

text: Jitter = (RTT(n) - RTT(n-1)I (average or maximum)
speaker: Simon

text: No timestamp field required
speaker: Simon

text: No support needed from the remote device
speaker: Simon

text: Y Easiest to implement, widely accepted in most RFPs.
speaker: Simon

text: 2. ICMP Timestamp-Based Jitter (Enhanced Payload Timestamp)
speaker: Simon

text: This method adds a custom timestamp field into the ICMP Echo payload.
speaker: Simon

text: Insert a sender-side timestamp into the ICMP payload
speaker: Simon

text: Remote device simply echoes back the payload
speaker: Simon

text: Use RTT and timestamp to compute jitter
speaker: Simon

text: Does not require any special support on the remote device
speaker: Simon

text: V Still easy to implement; suitable for professional-grade jitter measurement.
speaker: Simon

text: 3. Cisco-Style UDP Jitter (Full IP SLA Responder)
speaker: Simon

text: This method mimics Cisco IP SLA Jitter using UDP packets with timestamp information.
speaker: Simon

text: Requires both sender and responder to support the protocol
speaker: Simon

text: Parses timestamps for one-way delay and jitter
speaker: Simon

text: Measures packet loss, MOS, and detailed statistics
speaker: Simon

text: This is Cisco proprietary and not supported by most vendors
speaker: Simon
